questions.question: Which statement best defines the event-driven programming paradigm?

choices.statement: The program executes a fixed sequence of instructions defined entirely by the programmer in the main routine
The flow of the program is determined by events such as user actions, sensor outputs, or messages from other programs/threads
The program is organized only around mathematical functions with no state
The program runs once from start to finish with little or no user intervention

questions.hint: The program reacts to things happening instead of following a fixed script.

questions.question: In embedded systems, how can event-driven behavior be achieved without a constantly running main loop?

choices.statement: By using recursive procedures
By using anonymous inner classes
By using hardware interrupts
By using adapter classes

questions.hint: Hardware can interrupt the processor to signal that something happened.

questions.question: Before the arrival of object-oriented programming languages, how were event handlers typically implemented?

choices.statement: As subroutines within a procedural program, with execution flow controlled from the application's main routine
As listener objects registered with event sources
As lambda expressions passed to a scheduler
As adapter classes generated by an IDE

questions.hint: Listener objects did not exist yet; think of plain procedures.

questions.question: According to the text, which factor was one of the drivers behind the object-oriented approach that also pushed software toward event handling?

choices.statement: The decline of graphical user interfaces
The need to remove databases from information systems
The preference for command-line interfaces over windows

The rapid development and commercial adoption of database technology, which made the database the central component, with software providing a user interface and event-handling procedures for queries and updates

questions.hint: Think about how databases became central to business software.

questions.question: What is the role of the scheduler (dispatcher) in an event-driven application?

choices.statement: It writes the code for every event handler automatically
It runs continuously, receives a stream of events, determines each event's type, and passes it to the relevant event handler
It stores the data attributes of every object in the application
It converts event-driven code into procedural code before execution

questions.hint: It listens for events and hands each one to the right handler.

questions.question: In the pseudo-code scheduler, what may happen when the scheduler encounters an event for which no appropriate event handler exists?

choices.statement: The application is immediately terminated
The event is automatically converted into an EndProgram event
Depending on the nature of the event, the scheduler can ignore it or raise (throw) and exception
The scheduler restarts the main loop from the first event type

questions.hint: What would a sensible scheduler do with an event nobody handles?

questions.question: Why should care be taken when writing an event handler that triggers another event?

choices.statement: It could put the application into an infinite loop
Event handlers are not allowed to call other handlers in Java
It would permanently delete the scheduler
It prevents the user interface from being displayed

questions.hint: A handler that raises an event could end up triggering itself over and over.

questions.question: According to the text, the "state of the system" that event handlers often change encompasses which of the following?

choices.statement: Only the data stored in database fields
Only the appearance of the user interface
Only the list of registered event listeners
Both the data used by the system (e.g., a database field value) and the state of the user interface (e.g., which object has focus or a text box's background colour)

questions.hint: State covers more than what is visible on the screen.

questions.question: In Java Swing, when a user presses a JButton, which participant is the source of the event?

choices.statement: The ActionEvent object
The ActionListener object
The JButton, since it is the component that generates the event
The java.awt.event package

questions.hint: Which component is the one that actually generates the event when pressed?

questions.question: Which statement about the EventListener interface in the java.util package is correct?

choices.statement: It declares an actionPerformed() method that all listeners must implement
It is an abstract class that provides empty implementations of listener methods
It is a functional interface used only for lambda expressions
It is a marker interface with no methods that acts as the ancestor of all event listener interfaces

questions.hint: It has no methods; it only marks a family of interfaces.

A:click, A:click, B:click
A:click, B:click, A:click, B:click
A:click, A:click

questions.hint: The second click happens after the second listener has been added.

Which program produces the following output?

UI: save

Which program produces the following output?

Expected output:
Total clicks: 3

b.on(e -> System.out.println(e));
b.on(e -> { if (e.equals("click")) System.out.println(e); });
b.on(e -> { if (e.startsWith("c")) System.out.println(e.toUpperCase()); });

hs.remove(2);
hs.clear();
hs.remove(r2);

q.peekLast()
q.peek()
q.pollLast()

questions.question:
Which rule completes the program so that a matching event can trigger its corresponding response?

Expected query and result:
?- handle_event(button_pressed, Response).
Response = start_game.

event_response(button_pressed, start_game).
event_response(key_pressed, move_player).

handle_event(Event, Response) :-
    __________

choices.statement: event_response(Response, Event).
event_response(Event, Response).
Response = Event.
Event = Response.

questions.hint: Look up the response that goes with the event.

choices.statement: printf("%d\n", apply(square, 5));
printf("%d\n", apply(5, square));
printf("%d\n", square(apply));
printf("%d\n", apply(square(5), 5))

questions.hint: apply expects a function first and a value second.
